interpretation: Conventional reference approaches for task-relative novelty, not a map of model pretraining data or a historical novelty oracle.
gcd: Conventional reference: list common divisors, use Euclid's algorithm and the invariant gcd(a,b)=gcd(a,b-a), or use minimum prime exponents. Standard proofs that subtraction preserves the set of common divisors, their parameterized instances and routine scaling remain conventional. Reproving, restating or renaming these earns no novelty credit.
lcm: Conventional reference: search multiples, take maximum prime exponents, or use lcm(a,b)=a*b/gcd(a,b) for positive integers. Merely restating or renaming these earns no novelty credit.
polynomial_multiplication: Conventional reference: distribute factors, collect coefficients, use standard identities or coefficient convolution. Merely restating or renaming these earns no novelty credit.
dice: Conventional reference: enumerate equiprobable outcomes, use independence and product sample spaces, count with dynamic programming or multiply probability-generating polynomials. Merely restating or renaming these earns no novelty credit.
prime_factorization: Conventional reference: trial division, divisibility tests and uniqueness of prime decomposition. Merely restating or renaming these earns no novelty credit.
polynomial_equations: Conventional reference: factorization, standard low-degree formulas, substitution and finding all real roots with the stated rounding convention. Merely restating or renaming these earns no novelty credit.
largest_island: Conventional reference: identify connected components of the four-neighbor grid graph by flood fill, breadth/depth-first search or union-find and count their vertices. Renaming these algorithms earns no novelty credit.
simple_geometry: Conventional reference: triangulate a convex polygon to obtain the interior-angle sum (n-2)*180 degrees, or sum exterior turning angles to 360 degrees, then subtract known angles. Renaming these earns no novelty credit.
matrix_rank: Conventional reference: row reduction, pivot counting, linear independence, nonzero minors and the rank-nullity theorem. Renaming these earns no novelty credit.
modular_inverse: Conventional reference: enumerate residues or use extended Euclid/Bezout with gcd(a,m)=1 to find a multiplicative inverse modulo m. Renaming these earns no novelty credit.
